subject: ent
title: Maxillofacial fractures and CSF rhinorrhoea

steps.tx: Facial trauma triage protects airway (blood, swelling, displaced maxilla), cervical spine, eyes and brain before bones. **Zygomatic** fractures flatten cheek, restrict mouth opening (coronoid impingement), cause infraorbital numbness and diplopia from orbital floor involvement. Naso orbital ethmoid injuries telescope the nasal bridge with telecanthus. Mandible fractures (second commonest facial bone after nasal) malocclude, favour paired fractures (symphysis plus condyle ring), and threaten airway in bilateral parasymphyseal (flail, tongue falls back) injuries.
steps.say: Airway, spine, eyes, brain first. Flat cheek plus numb plus trismus is zygoma. Broken jaw breaks in two places.

steps.tx: **Le Fort** midface fractures separate facial skeleton at levels: I low transverse above teeth (floating palate), II pyramidal through infraorbital rims and nasal bridge, III craniofacial disjunction through zygomatic arches and orbits (floating face). All can bleed massively and obstruct airway; mobile maxilla on examination (gentle, once) and malocclusion with CSF leak risk (cribriform in II or III) define them. CT facial bones with 3D reconstruction plans fixation restoring occlusion first, then buttresses.
steps.say: Le Fort one floats palate, two floats nose pyramid, three floats whole face. Fix occlusion first.

steps.tx: **Orbital blowout** fractures floor (or medial wall) into sinuses after blunt globe injury, trapping inferior rectus causing diplopia worse on upgaze, enophthalmos later, infraorbital numbness and oculocardiac bradycardia in children (trapdoor white eyed blowout needs urgent release). Urgent indications: muscle entrapment, large floor defect with enophthalmos risk, retrobulbar haemorrhage (orbital compartment syndrome with proptosis, tense globe, vision loss needing lateral canthotomy). Retrobulbar bleed must not wait for CT when vision threatened.
steps.say: Child cannot look up, feels sick and slow pulse after eye hit: trapdoor, operate urgently. Tight proptosed eye bleeding behind globe: cut canthus now.

steps.tx: **CSF rhinorrhoea** follows anterior skull base fractures (cribriform, frontal sinus posterior table, sphenoid) presenting as clear watery unilateral discharge increasing leaning forward, salty taste, reservoir sign, confirmed by beta 2 transferrin (not glucose strips). Most traumatic leaks close within a week with head elevation and avoiding straining or nose blowing; persistent, recurrent meningitis or large defects need endoscopic repair. Prophylactic antibiotics do not prevent meningitis and are generally withheld. Beta trace protein is alternative test where available.
steps.say: Clear watery nose drip after head injury is CSF until beta 2 transferrin says no. Most seal in a week sitting up.
